Module 1:  Agency, education and innovation (1 hour)

Position of the majority of young [sex of FGD] on the ladder of power and freedom (private rating): 5 = Power and freedom to make almost all major life decisions: 0 votes; 4 = Power and freedom to make many major life decisions: 10 votes; 3 = Power and freedom to make some major life decisions: 0 votes; 2 = Only a small amount of power and freedom: 0 votes; 1 = Almost no power or freedom to make decisions: 0 votes
After completing schooling our abilities to make decisions have increased. Today I can propose something to my parents and I am listened to.

[Another one?] We live at home after studies we are forced to decide what activities to do because during the time we were still studying we majorly depended on parents and other relatives for our needs. For now they see us free so we are eligible to work.

The children we have force us to make decisions in life. Having given birth to a child you have to decide and work hard because a child will see other children taking juice or sweets and he wants you to buy him the same. If you have no money the child will cry. You cannot allow her to keep on crying every day instead you need to have some money. This makes us make decision to do petty business.
Globalization also contributed to our power to make decision.

[How?] Today we are able to receive information through the mobile phones in that if you want an advice or a support from someone, you can get answered there and then and decide to change the direction or try to other people different from the past whereby you had to send a letter through the postal office and it takes a month to get answered.

Without education everything will be difficult to you. For me I think it is better for one to get to school at least get to know how to read and write. Even if you don’t go further in studies but at least one is able to solve small issues that are within her capacities.

[Another one?] Education creates competition among people when they see people who have studied doing well in life. The wish becoming like them and given opportunities to study they do study hard and attain their goals.
Education has liberated us from ignorance. The business I do today it is because I have been to school so I am able to determine a profit and loss.
Education creates an understanding to use. We are able to solve certain conflicts in the community amicably because we have understood that chaos is not good.
Many of the boys today complete form four and some of them get to continue to form five and six whereas some complete university level.
[Do we all agree with her?] All respondents: Yes.
[And girls? Until what grade do boys generally study in this community?] These also end at form four.
Some of them have been able to go further to the university and other vocational training institutions.
[Do we all agree with them?] All respondents: Yes.
[What level of education do you think boys should have in this village?] They should study to the university level.
It is not bad if they study and become teachers.
[What level of education do you think girls should have in this village?] To the university.
After completing the university at least one can start struggling to find a job.
Both boys and girls are given a priority in as far as education is concerned.
Today the government forces the parents to take all children that have reached the age to go to school or the children who have succeeded to join secondary school studies.
Parents who fail to take children to school it is because of failure to afford the school needs.
[What different agricultural activities do girls learn about when they are young in this community?] Farming activities such as preparing of the farm, planting, weeding and harvesting.
We do learn how to grow maize, pigeon peas and other crops.
[Is there any other activity that girls learn about agricultural activities when they are young?] All respondents are quiet.

[Which of these new agricultural practices have been the most important for young women like you in this community?] All respondents come to a common understanding that the introduction of new maize, rice and tomato varieties as well as the introduction of irrigation farming have been the most important new agricultural practices for the young women in this community.
[Why important?] The introduction of new tomato varieties has provided employment to many people who are engaged in tomato growing.
The new maize and rice varieties lead to rich harvest. For this case therefore, people are able to store enough food as well as earn an income.
This area experiences draught but because we are along the river, the introduction of irrigation farming enables people to do the farming throughout the year.
The new tomato varieties grow within three months. People are able to get money within a short period of time.
All respondents: Yes.
[Why?] These opportunities are open to each member of the community.
All men and women are engaged in farming activities so every opportunity the relates to improving the way they do their activities concerns them all.

[How?] Difficult tasks such as the clearing the bushes before land preparation are normally done by men and women do come in to do the rest of the activities.
Sometimes when women are doing the weeding or planting men are busy making bricks so as to earn an additional income in the household.
Instead this can be good because he would be able to sell crops harvested to construct a house if at all he has good plans and not luxurious.
If at all he is strategic, farming can enable him to fight against poverty.

[Is it easy for him to grow maize on his own with no difficulties?] During the past years parents used to prevent them but now parents find that they cannot fulfill all the needs of their children so they give them freedom to go trying farming on their own.
[What difficulties are they likely to face?] They might face a problem of lacking land where to carry out the farming as well as money to buy the farm inputs.
[Another one?] They are also likely to face a problem of finding a better market for their crops.
[Would they be asked by their parents to give out the share of the produce for home consumption?] All respondents: Yes.
There are very few young women who can do the farming on their own?

[Why?] Like us girls we are seen as contributors to household labor and domestic needs so we have no time to prepare and plant our own maize farms. We end up participating in planting the household farms.
[Another one?] Even for a girl to get the land on which to do the farming is difficult.
[How do young men manage getting land on which to do the farming?] The boys are able to go working even to the Chinese company and save the money that can enable them rent land.
If it happened that a woman rented her own plot and a man also rented his own, they will decide to first work at one’s plot as a family and then they will turn to the other one’s farm.

[Could this vary based on seasons or crops?] During brick making season for example a man can leave a woman to work with other family members and for him he goes to do brick making activities or caring for other gardens such as tomato gardens.

This will depend on how they do their activities. If they are used of assisting each other, she will work in her husband’s farm. Because all the crops belong to the household, I think she will assist.
All respondents: Yes.
[Which kind of labor that is normally available when needed?] Mainly human labor together with tractors all of which need one to have money.
All respondents: Yes.
[Which responsibilities are these?] The farming season might reach when a young woman is pregnant or sick.

Taking care of children. You find that during farming season a woman is supposed to wake up early and go farming but if at all she has children, she will have to care for them by preparing tea and meals for them before she can set off for the farm. This sometimes delays her. There is a saying that says “ a lazy person’s farm does well whereas a sick persons’ firm is badly off” meaning that it is better to be lazy and prepare a small farm than preparing a small farm and get sick or have a burden of caring for children.
[Another one?] Also one might be taking care of the sick family members or going to work to other farms to earn income.
She will need to have money because you cannot get someone from his or her responsibilities to assist you without paying him or her.
[Another one?] Apart from using the household members, she has no any other alternative other than paying people to assist her.
Some women do preserve maize and rice to exchange with people who will work for them during farming season.
It is only through paying people to work for them or with the agreement to receive materials such as food in form of maize or rice.
All respondents: Yes.
[Whom does she need to consult?] She can plan with her husband or other household members.
[Who else does she need to consult?] No one apart from the agricultural extension officer.
All respondents: Yes.

[Another one?] Adam will refuse her because he is rigid that women cannot plan and own money.

Mary has a bad reputation and people think that Mary has bewitched Mark by feeding him with traditional medicine commonly known as (Rimbwata)

[Another one?] Mary will never be respected by the community members even if they respect each other as couples. Because of the traditions, the community will worry about the life style of these two couples.
For the friends who have an understanding about life difficulties will have no problem with Mary because they know she is fighting to use her talents in business to raise the household’s income.
[Another one?] If it was in Zanzibar the friends would have no problem with Mark because there it is normal for men to do domestic activities but our traditions here do not permit this.
The friends will disrespect Mark and they can no longer seek any advice from him as they consider him as a person to sit among men.
Mark will be happy.
[Why?] Because he agreed to stay at home. This means he is convinced of Mary’s enterprise.
People will consider the success as belonging to Mary because Mark remained at home as Mary went working.
Mark is now thinking of what will happen in the future. In our traditions it is a man who posses wealth and women just participate in it but for this case it is Mary possessing.
It means that if a man attends school, women must attend school too.

[Another one?] It means that for the decision making in the household be done by both a man and a woman together. If at all they are to go in the farm but a woman had another task somewhere, it means that a man must listen to her.
[Do you think gender equality is a good or a bad thing?] All respondents: It is good.

[Why?] It means that a man and woman share 50% each in decision making and possessing wealth as well as employment opportunities. Today even women are involved in night watch guards positions as well as military training.

During the past you could find a woman carrying a child at her back, a hand hoe at the shoulders, and firewood on her head while a man walked empty handed. After reaching at home, a woman has to prepare water for the man to wash the hands. Today however, most of the families men and women share activities in a process to assist one another.

[Why do you think that there are some women who do not move freely on their own in the village?] Some women cannot move freely in the village because of their husbands’ way of living. There are men who never like seeing their wives moving the way they like in the village.

It becomes easy for them to move if they discuss with their parents and the parents get convinced to whom they are going to. Parents normally hesitate allowing their daughters to move to towns if they have no relatives there. They fear of their security. For the boys if they are old already at least they can fight for their rights when in town but not to girls.
[Do many young women from here migrate to towns and cities?] They do go to towns some go to work as house girls but some move to their relatives.
Normally people have a negative attitude towards a girl who has moved to town and returned in the village.
[Why?] In most of the time these people tend to return when they have changed their traditional ways of doing things. They have different dressing styles that are not allowed in the society.
The community thinks that these people were practicing prostitution.
It is better is she returns with some positive changes like building a house or purchasing a plot. If not, it becomes worse as people consider her as a failure.
[What opportunities do they normally have?] They never have any big difference apart from the new ways of dressing and setting hair (as other respondents get into laughter)

[What changes would you like to see in the village for the young men?] Small industries are needed so as to create employment opportunities to young men.
The government should introduce free or low charge trainings on different activities that can create employment such as poultry keeping and soap making.

[What changes would you like to see in the village for the young women?] At home for example we normally keep poultry to sell eggs and chicks but there is no market for these chicks so we need the market where we can supply poultry products.

Even at home we do have milk that has no market. Sometimes you find us keeping about twenty litres which we end up using it for home consumption. We therefore need a good market with good prices for dairy products.
[Another one?] Also girls need employment opportunities. We need working places so that we can earn more incomes to support our families.
Entrepreneur skills also could be important for so that girls can set up personal enterprises.
